messages:
maria: heads up — I'm starting a controlled loadstory to compare kernel selection + kv warmup behavior across quant profiles. goal: clear apples-vs-oranges complaints and get a reproducible recipe for the regression gate.

sam: SGTM. can you paste the run config? want to make sure synthetic traffic vs replay params are explicit.

maria: config below. replay harness = recorded 95th-percentile arrival pattern from prod (region-eu), synthetic = poisson with same mean qps. warmup: 120s prefill + 60s steady. models: gpt-small-16k (fp16), gpt-small-16k-8bit, gpt-small-16k-4bit-q -- kernel selection flags toggled (auto/manual). batching: dynamic with 8ms window cap; also test fixed batch sizes 1/4/8/16. kv cache: cold, prewarmed, and adaptive-evict off/on. speculative decoding: off / topk-2 speculative / topk-4 speculative. regression gate threshold: +10% p99 or +5% quality drop.

maria: ```
bench.repeat=3
traffic.replay.file=s3://redwood-replays/eu/q95_2026-03-01.json
traffic.synthetic.distribution=poisson
qps.target=120
seq_len=1024
model.variants=[fp16,8bit,4bit-q]
kernel.selection=[auto,force_flash,force_triton]
batching.window_ms=8
kv.prefill_seconds=120
kv.policy=[cold,prewarm,adaptive]
speculative=[off,topk2,topk4]
quality.eval_set=sanity-smoke-200
reggate.p99_delta=+10%
reggate.quality_delta=-5%
```

jeff: couple quick asks — 1) when you say "force_triton" are we running the Triton backend path or our in-house fused kernels? need clarity for result attribution. 2) will the bench capture per-token CPU/GPU breakdowns and kernel-level counters?

maria: 1) `force_triton` = route to Triton shim (no fused kernels). `force_flash` = fused attention path. `auto` lets the kernel selector choose based on heuristics. 2) yes: we collect per-kernel latency histogram, BF16/FP16 ops counters, GPU utilization, and CPU for batching thread. also kv hit/miss counters and avg kv latency.

ana: FYI the last time we ran a similar sweep we saw a weird p99 hump when kv miss rate hit ~12% and batching window was small. suspect contention on async copy path. we should instrument copy queues.

sam: can we capture a short flame for the slow case? also add `CUDA_MEMCHECK=0` :P joking but we need lightweight stack traces — callstack sampling every 5ms for 30s.

maria: added callstack sampling and a micro-trace config. also will dump kernel occupancy and SM stall reasons for slow runs.

perf-ci-bot: benchmark started: id=bench-2026-03-17-1793001234, config=controlled-loadstory-kernel-sweep, expected ~2h. logs -> https://ci.redwood.ai/bench/bench-2026-03-17-1793001234

rachel: note on quality eval: use both exact-match on eval prompts and CE-based score for distribution drift. speculative decoding can increase early divergence — track prefix perplexity delta over first 50 tokens.

jeff: good point. add `prefix_ppl.delta` and `first50.bleu` (approx).

maria: result notes (first pass, synthetic Poisson vs replay): synthetic shows slightly higher throughput (expected) but underestimates p99 by ~8% compared to replay when KV misses are injected. auto-kernel chose fused path 72% of time for fp16, but switched to Triton on 4bit-q more often.

maria: here's a short paste of the perf table (median over repeats) — rough numbers:
```
model   kernel    batching   kv_mode   qps   p50(ms)  p95(ms)  p99(ms)  kv_miss%  spec=topk2_quality_delta
fp16    auto      dynamic    prewarm   118   18       46       92       1.2       -0.4%
8bit    force_flash dynamic  adaptive  112   20       52       115      3.8       -0.9%
4bit-q  force_triton fixed8    cold      95    26       88       210      14.3      -2.7%
```

sam: 4bit-q + cold kv + triton path looks bad on p99 — kv miss + small batch amplify tail. can we rerun with kv prewarm and dynamic batching?

maria: did that in repeat 2: same model/quant with prewarm + dynamic batching got p99 -> 130ms and q delta -> -1.1%. So big chunk of regression is KV warmup + kernel mismatch.

ana: interestingly, speculative topk2 recovered ~20% of throughput for 4bit-q but worsened quality on a shotgun prompt set (some hallucinations). we should flag speculative as opt-in behind regression gate.

jeff: propose a simple regression gate for dedicated: block rollout if p99 increases > 12% or quality drop > 2% on the eval set. for spec decoding, require additional A/B and human review for >1% quality degradation.

maria: +1. I'll draft a PR that adds the gate rule, the bench harness config, and the runbook for triage (how to interpret kernel selector traces, where to look for copy queue stalls).

rachel: for the runbook, include command snippets to reproduce the slow trace locally, e.g.:
```bash
# reproduce slow case (4bit-q, cold kv, force_triton)
python tools/bench_runner.py --replay s3://redwood-replays/eu/q95_2026-03-01.json \
  --model gpt-small-16k-4bit-q --kernel force_triton --kv-policy cold \
  --batching dynamic --speculative off --outdir /tmp/bench-repro && tail -n 200 /tmp/bench-repro/log.txt
```

maria: putting results + raw traces into the artifact bucket now. I'll ping when uploads complete.

maria: next steps: 1) PR for regression gate + bench config 2) follow-up microbench for async copy path 3) spec-decoding gating policy. filing tickets now.
